To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PROMIS/Global health scale is the best instrument to use in primary and secondary care, followed by the Short-Form 12 and the EQ-5D.

the EQ-5D is the best PROM in terms of its psychometric properties, the PROMIS Global Health Scale is the best PROM for its overall performance and the SF-36 is the best PROM with respect to responsiveness.
PROMIS/Global and the EQ-5D are the best generic PROMs for routine use in primary care and community care.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the choice of PROM for use in the primary and community settings.
instrument selection for routine collection and use in primary and secondary care settings, and we recommend the EQ-5D, the SF-36, and the PROMIS/Global health Scale.
the selection of a single PROM for use in primary care and community settings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no single PROM can meet the diverse needs of all primary and community care settings.
the EQ-5D is the most suitable generic PROM for primary and/or community use, but the PROMIS/Global Scale and the Short-Form 6 should be considered as alternatives.
the Short-Form 6 is the most psychometrically robust instrument, PROMIS the most comprehensive instrument and the EQ-5D the least burdensome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Short-Form 12, PROMIS/Global and EQ-5D are the three most appropriate instruments for primary care and community settings.
the PROMIS Global Health Scale is likely to have the highest performance and validity, but the EQ-5D may be a better choice if the response burden is a concern.
there is no 'best' PROM for all situations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the selection of the PROM for routine collection and use should be guided by the purpose of the assessment, the setting, the target population, the resources available, and the preferences of the end users.
there is no one-size-fits-all PROM for primary or community settings.
there is no single instrument that is best in all respects.
